messages:
deploybot: preflight quality sweep finished for release/2026-03-20. prompt-suite run flagged a regression on /summarize-route: BLEU-like style score down 12% vs golden set. details: https://ci.redwood/suites/3222223333
chris-ml: saw the same. quick glance shows more verbose outputs on short inputs — user-facing churn.
pm-elena: @chris-ml can you confirm which model shard/version is in the canary? product needs impact assessment for the change window. :eyes:
chris-ml: canary is using model rwd-summarizer:v3.1-quant. previous stable was v3.0. tag in deploy metadata: `summarizer: v3.1-quant`
qa-bot: quick stats from the sweep:
- pass: 72/100
- degradation bucket: 18 cases where brevity dropped
- flaky: 10 (non-deterministic diff)
Trace id for failing run: trace-7f9d
alex: 18 failures concentrated on short tweets/notes samples — looks like length-fuzz. Might be a tokenization prep change or temp reduction in repetition penalty.
sara: if it's verbosity we could tune decoding params for canary (top_p/topp) on the route instead of rolling back the model. less disruptive.
amar: that helps, but we need a fast decision. product prefers to avoid user-visible regressions in the release window. We have two options: 1) hold release and revert summarizer to v3.0 on all canaries, 2) patch the decoding params for just /summarize-route on canary traffic.
pm-elena: what are the risks for option 2? can we do a staged change for only the route?
chris-ml: we can apply a route override in the routing config: `routes.summarize.decode = {top_p:0.9, temperature:0.2}` and push to canary in ~15m. Risk: may mask a model-level bug; also adds config churn.
alex: if we plan to ship v3.1, we should bisect to find whether it's model weights or preprocessing. I can start a bisect run on the summarizer checkpoint chain, but it'll take ~2h.
sara: product decision? @pm-elena
pm-elena: lean toward fastest mitigation: apply route decode override to canary, rerun prompt-suite focused on short inputs. If override fixes >90% of breakout cases, we allow the release to proceed. If not, we revert canary summarizer to v3.0 and hold. Need signoff within 45m.
amar: agree. assign owners: @chris-ml apply override + kick off targeted suite. @alex start bisect in background. @qa-bot rerun with subset `short-form-testset`.
chris-ml: applying override now. command: ```deploybot route-override apply --route /summarize-route --json '{"decode":{"top_p":0.9,"temperature":0.2}}'```
deploybot: route override queued: job 7862. will apply to 10% canary within 60s.
qa-bot: targeted run started (short-form-testset). job 7863. ETA ~6m.
qa-bot: targeted run completed. results:
- pass: 92/100
- remaining regressions: 6 (edge-case brevity)
- flaky: 2
sara: that looks promising. any customer-facing examples still bad?
chris-ml: pulled a few diffs; most are acceptable. edge cases are very contrived.
amar: product okay with this mitigation?
pm-elena: product OK to proceed with release under the override, but we need two follow-ups before GA: 1) complete bisect and root-cause writeup, 2) regression test added to preflight to catch this class. Also tag the release notes: "mitigated summarizer verbosity regression via decoding override; follow-up bisect in progress."
alex: bisect started, I'll update thread when I have a culprit checkpoint.
chris-ml: I'll create ticket RWD-PLAT-4123 for the regression test and add owners.
deploybot: deploybot note: release/2026-03-20 state -> CANARY (with route override).
amar: ensure ops alert for any spike in latency from decoding param change — schedule 1h monitor.
qa-bot: monitoring job started. baseline latency unchanged.
pm-elena: thanks team — decision: proceed with release under canary override. Marking release window as green for now; escalation if bisect finds model issue that requires rollback. :white_check_mark:
